findings.topic: Rep ranges / rest for strength goal, intermediate lifter
findings.summary: For a primarily strength-oriented goal, intermediate lifters typically benefit from heavier loads in the ~3-6 rep range on main compound lifts with 2-3 minutes rest, supplemented by moderate-rep accessory work (8-12 reps) with shorter rest.
findings.source: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed. (periodization chapter summary)

findings.summary: For people with shoulder impingement symptoms, strict overhead barbell/dumbbell pressing is commonly cited as a provocative movement; landmine presses (angled, partial range) and flat/incline horizontal pressing are frequently recommended as better-tolerated substitutes while still training the same muscle groups.
findings.source: Physiopedia: Shoulder Impingement Syndrome — exercise considerations (summary)

findings.summary: An upper/lower split run twice per week (4 total sessions) is a well-supported structure at the intermediate stage, allowing higher per-session focus and recovery between repeats of the same muscle groups compared to full-body, while still hitting each pattern twice weekly.
findings.source: NSCA Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning, 4th ed. (program design chapter summary)
